about: Authored query pairs on Oracle Sales History for tools/sample_db_bench.py. label: 'equivalent' or 'different' under the declared keys minus 'drop' (not_null:T.c, pk:T, fk:T.c). A 'different' pair carries a witness: 'real' (the two queries already differ on the SH data) or a small database (missing columns are completed with legal values) that satisfies the remaining declarations and separates them. 'sibling' names the pair it negates. The fact tables sales and costs have no declared key (upstream declares none: sales' own comment says its rows are identified by the combination of all foreign keys, which is not a constraint), so pairs that would need one are labelled different. Most fact-table pairs filter the fact table to channel 9 (2,074 sales rows) or one day so that the real-data check stays small.

pairs.right: SELECT prod_id, amount_sold FROM sales WHERE channel_id = 9

pairs.label: equivalent

pairs.label: equivalent

pairs.why: a sale with no amount is on neither side
pairs.left: SELECT cust_id FROM sales WHERE channel_id = 9 AND amount_sold > 100 UNION ALL SELECT cust_id FROM sales WHERE channel_id = 9 AND amount_sold <= 100
pairs.right: SELECT cust_id FROM sales WHERE channel_id = 9

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: 17,506 customers have no marital status and are on neither side
pairs.left: SELECT cust_id FROM customers WHERE cust_marital_status = 'married' UNION ALL SELECT cust_id FROM customers WHERE cust_marital_status <> 'married'
pairs.right: SELECT cust_id FROM customers

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: prod_id is NOT NULL on both sides, so INTERSECT and IN agree on NULL
pairs.left: SELECT prod_id FROM sales WHERE channel_id = 9 INTERSECT DISTINCT SELECT prod_id FROM costs WHERE channel_id = 9
pairs.right: SELECT DISTINCT prod_id FROM sales WHERE channel_id = 9 AND prod_id IN (SELECT prod_id FROM costs WHERE channel_id = 9)

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: INTERSECT treats two NULLs as equal and IN does not
pairs.left: SELECT cust_marital_status FROM customers INTERSECT DISTINCT SELECT cust_marital_status FROM customers WHERE cust_year_of_birth > 1990
pairs.right: SELECT DISTINCT cust_marital_status FROM customers WHERE cust_marital_status IN (SELECT cust_marital_status FROM customers WHERE cust_year_of_birth > 1990)

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: cust_id is NOT NULL on both sides
pairs.left: SELECT cust_id FROM customers EXCEPT DISTINCT SELECT cust_id FROM sales
pairs.right: SELECT DISTINCT c.cust_id FROM customers AS c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sales AS s WHERE s.cust_id = c.cust_id)

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: an IN subquery and the correlated EXISTS
pairs.left: SELECT prod_id FROM products WHERE prod_id IN (SELECT prod_id FROM sales WHERE channel_id = 9)
pairs.right: SELECT p.prod_id FROM products AS p WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sales AS s WHERE s.prod_id = p.prod_id AND s.channel_id = 9)

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: country_id is countries' primary key, so the join repeats no customer
pairs.left: SELECT cust_id FROM customers WHERE country_id IN (SELECT country_id FROM countries WHERE country_region = 'Europe')
pairs.right: SELECT c.cust_id FROM customers AS c JOIN countries AS k ON c.country_id = k.country_id WHERE k.country_region = 'Europe'

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without countries' primary key two European rows with one id repeat the customer
pairs.left: SELECT cust_id FROM customers WHERE country_id IN (SELECT country_id FROM countries WHERE country_region = 'Europe')
pairs.right: SELECT c.cust_id FROM customers AS c JOIN countries AS k ON c.country_id = k.country_id WHERE k.country_region = 'Europe'

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: a product has many sales: the join repeats it
pairs.left: SELECT prod_id FROM products WHERE prod_id IN (SELECT prod_id FROM sales WHERE channel_id = 9)
pairs.right: SELECT p.prod_id FROM products AS p JOIN sales AS s ON s.prod_id = p.prod_id WHERE s.channel_id = 9

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: a filter on the partition column keeps whole partitions, so the ranks do not change
pairs.left: SELECT prod_id, prod_category, r FROM (SELECT prod_id, prod_category, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY prod_category ORDER BY prod_list_price DESC) AS r FROM products) AS t WHERE prod_category = 'Golf'
pairs.right: SELECT prod_id, prod_category, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY prod_category ORDER BY prod_list_price DESC) AS r FROM products WHERE prod_category = 'Golf'

pairs.label: different

pairs.left: SELECT prod_id, prod_category, r FROM (SELECT prod_id, prod_category, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY prod_category ORDER BY prod_list_price DESC) AS r FROM products) AS t WHERE prod_id > 100
